newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Dornbusch says devalued Brazil real mistake - paper.
newsitem.headline: Dornbusch says devalued Brazil real mistake - paper.

text.p: U.S.-based economist Rudiger Dornbusch said it would be a "terrible mistake" to devaluate the Brazilian currency given the size of the fiscal deficit and the level of economic opening, a financial newspaper said.

"I would say the real is 30-percent overvalued. But if nothing is done in the fiscal area and the economy doesn't open up more, it would be a terrible mistake to carry out a strong devaluation," Dornbusch told Gazeta Mercantil during an interview at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland. "This would only create an enormous instability."
Dornbusch believes once the government's accounts are balanced, the currency could be devalued to stimulate exports which are essential for Brazilian economic growth, Gazeta said.
He said a mere adjustment in the exchange band system, as based on the Chilean model for example, would not be sufficient to promote export growth, Gazeta said.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
